Ok, to start off I'd like to say I've been playing football for many many years. I've played in a range of positions, including RB, CB, CDM, CM and recently, I've been playing striker. I've read a lot of football guides over the years, had incredible training from some incredible coaches and most importantly, I've enjoyed practicing and playing. In this guide I will cover the basics of football and outline how you can improve.

  1. The most obvious way to improve - Practice. There's no way around this one. The longer you spend kicking the ball around the better you will become, its simple. However, there are ways to get the most out of the time you have. Firstly, try to complete a range of drills including shooting, passing, dribbling and your touch. Even if your position does not normally call for, shooting for example, still train it. Try to touch the ball for at least an hour a day, even if its just in your garden don't underestimate the power juggling the ball has or simply passing the ball against a wall.

  2. Fitness is another important part of becoming a better footballer - The most important components of fitness for football is; speed, stamina, strength and agility. A strong core will make it harder for your opponent to push you off the ball. Good agility and quick feet will make you a nightmare for defenders. Get down to the gym, go for a run and bust out some cones and do some agility work.

  3. Following on from the last point, a hugely discarded point is eating right. If you are truly dedicated to becoming a better footballer you should put in the effort to eat clean. Eat a lot of protein, drink a lot of water and especially before a game make sure your body is fueled up with enough energy so you can put in 100%.

  4. One of the best tips I've received. Slow down your game. Take an extra second to control the ball, look around and make a better pass instead of hitting it away as soon as you get the ball. You want to have the ball as much as you can when you're playing, don't shy away from asking for a pass. As soon as I slowed down my game I become 10x better.

  5. Don't bottle tackles and don't ever not try during a game. Easy enough, coaches love it when they see people giving their best whether in training or in a match. This could be the difference between getting picked or not, despite your technical abilities.

  6. First touch - One of the most important skills a footballer can have. A good first touch can help getting past a player, it can set you up for shooting or it can help stop your team conceding. Get outside and kick the ball as high as you can and work on touching it down. If the ball comes from above try to pull your foot down with the ball. If the ball comes foot high try to control with the side of your foot.

  7. Shooting and passing - If you have a cones set up a marker away from you, work on passing the ball to it from different positions, after controlling the ball. Move the cone away and repeat. Shooting is easier to train. If you have a goal just practice shooting at it. Again from different positions, after controlling the ball and also get someone to roll the ball to you and hit it quickly.

  8. Dribbling and skills - Dribbling is one of the most important functions for a winger, the ability to beat a player, however, is needed no matter what position you play. Dribble through cones and practice going past a player. Skills are recognized by every footballer and are often used as an indicator as to how good a player is. I disagree with this but nonetheless skills can be useful in the right circumstances. Remember though - if you aren't perfect with the skill in training, don't attempt it in a game! Failing to complete a skill looks foolish and makes you look like a bad player.

  9. Work on your weak areas - Most amateur players are one footed. Train with your other foot in every session. This goes for your other weaknesses, there are no excuses. Practice passing, shooting and controlling the ball with your weak foot. Also practice penalties, free kicks and corners. You never know when you might need to use it.

  10. Johan Cryuff once said, "On average, a footballer has the ball for an average of 3 minutes a match. What a player does for those other 87 minutes is what makes him great player instead of a good player." This is extremely important for those who want to improve, look for those opportunities where you can receive the ball. Watch professional games and study players in your position to see their mannerisms and how they perform on and off the ball.

Thanks for reading this guide, if you have any tips I haven't mentioned feel free to post them in the comments.
